findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed fly tape to be mounted on the ceiling above food preparation and storage areas. The PIC was informed and plans to move the tapes to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure fly tapes are mounted away from food preparation and storage spaces.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. Ensure staff are using the provided paper towels to turn off the hand sink to avoid cross-contamination. An employee was also observed using their clothing to dry their hands after washing. Clothing poses a cross-contamination risk and therefore cannot be used for drying.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the hand sink in the bakery area to be obstructed. PIC was informed that hand sinks need to be accessible at all times to promote proper hand washing. The hand sink obstruction was removed during the inpsection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket next to the drive-thru window to have 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the concentration was too low, and the sanitizer bucket was replaced. Sanitizer concentrations will decrease over time with use and evaporation. Therefore, the sanitizer buckets need to be replaced frequently to ensure proper concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed multiple large storage containers holding white powders to be unlabeled. PIC was informed that labels need to be placed on containers to allow for recognition of container contents. Ensure containers are labeled by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the shelves of the syrup dispensers to have a heavy accumulation of syrup and dust. PIC stated that the dispensers are cleaned every Thursday. PIC was advised that cleaning frequency may need to be increased to avoid the accumulation of soil and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed employee food items stored on upper shelving of cooler above food for the consumer. PIC was advised that a designated storage area should be assigned below food for consumers to avoid cross-contamination. Ensure designated areas are assigned and in use prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed employee pour syrup down drain of kitchen hand sink. Advised employee that hand washing sinks may only be used for hand washing purposes. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizing solution available for use during food preparation and service. Sanitizing solution was made during inspection, and tested at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed containers used to store clean cooking utensils to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize containers used to store clean cooking utensils. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

The sanitizer in the bucket at bakery was at 0ppm upon arrival. The facility emptied the bucket and replaced it with a fresh sanitation bucket. The violation is considered corrected at the time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). 

Observed milks and tea concentrates in the coolers with no date marking. Mark containers that are open, at the end of the night, with the date they were opened and use or discard within 7 days. The concentrates were date marked. 
Develope a habit of proper date marking. Violation is considered corrected at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

Observed quiche on the speed rack cooling. The quiche was 157F. When asked, the employees stated that the quiche is left to sit on the speed rack until it reaches room temperature and then is placed into the cooler. The temperature of the Quiche was taken at approximately  30 to 45 minutes later and the quiche had dropped to 141F. The quiche was moved to the cooler and is 115F. 
The violation is considered to be corrected on site as the facility was walked through the cooling process during the inspection.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Wiping cloths at the bakery are hanging over the edge of the bucket. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer between uses.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-502.13: (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be reused. (B) The bulk milk container dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than one inch protruding from the chilled dispensing head. 
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Single use straws at the drive up window are exposed to potential contamination with personal items and handling practices. Cut down box for single use straws so that the straws can be provided to the customer without contaminating the lip-contact area of the straw.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed a wood rack for the storage of syrup bottles to have areas of raw wood. Seal the rack so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed rack of syrup bottles to be soiled with sugar. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to turn off faucet handles without a barrier such as a paper towel after appropriately washing hands with water and soap. Ensure staff is aware to use a barrier to turn off the faucets after hand washing - cross contamination of hands. Discussed with employee and PIC. COS.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved. 

Observed multiple ice scoop handles to be within the ice basins. Discussed with PIC and employees. Ensure the ice scoop handles stay upright in the ice to avoid cross contamination. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas of the facility that are in need of repair (must be smooth and easily cleanable, non-absorbent):
1. Mop sink needs caulked to the wall and around the base of the sink to the floor. Caulk the mop sink.
2. Seal the wood shelving in the prep kitchen area (baking supplies on shelving) and on all wood shelving in the upstairs dry storage. The ply wood is bare wood - must be sealed with a sealant or painted (top and edges). 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.
